dataset.title: GRIN research connections — published variant evidence
dataset.description: Selected GRIN2A/GRIN2B research cohorts: six Likely LoF variants, one provisional Possible LoF case and three controls. Real source facts; expert interpretation pending. Research planning only.
curation_notes: Machine-checked source transcription is not expert scientific review.
The existing GRIN connection and registry are acknowledged; the contribution is source-traceable research preparation.
No treatments, trial eligibility or access permissions are inferred.
S541G has a source cDNA/protein discrepancy and remains protein-level control evidence.

clinical_association.evidence_location: Chen 2020 Table 1, row 6; original disease-linked studies listed there include Lesca 2013, Swanger 2016, and Addis 2017.
clinical_association.note: Clinical features are reported patient associations in the cited literature; functional assay data do not establish clinical severity.

functional_evidence.evidence_location: Table 2, GRIN2A-p.Gly483Arg row; Table 3, same variant row.
functional_evidence.assay: Agonist concentration-response by two-electrode voltage clamp; deactivation and peak current by whole-cell voltage clamp.
functional_evidence.model: Recombinant human GluN1/GluN2A receptors in Xenopus laevis oocytes for agonist EC50; HEK293 cells for τw and peak amplitude.

predicted_charge_transfer.evidence_location: Swanger 2016 Table 3; ratios are author-calculated from measured receptor properties.

functional_evidence.uncertainty_note: Mean ± SEM unless confidence interval explicitly shown; sample sizes are assay observations, not participant counts.

integrated_function.evidence_location: Discussion, paragraph applying the framework to previously published variants (Supplementary Tables S3–S5).
integrated_function.why: Large reduction in glutamate potency, deactivation/current measurements and both predicted charge-transfer ratios; independently listed as Likely LoF by the multi-assay framework.

context_caveats: Recombinant diheteromeric receptor assay; not a neuronal or patient-level measurement.

clinical_association.evidence_location: Xu 2024 Table 1, row 40; Platzer 2017 clinical table also reports severe ID, seizures, MCD, and CVI.

functional_evidence.evidence_location: Tables 2–3, GluN2B-A639V row; Figure 5 summarizes classification criteria.
functional_evidence.assay: Agonist and Mg2+ concentration-response, pH sensitivity, surface expression, channel open probability, deactivation and current amplitude.
functional_evidence.model: Recombinant GluN1/GluN2B diheteromeric NMDARs expressed in Xenopus laevis oocytes and HEK cells.
functional_evidence.uncertainty_note: Mean ± SEM unless confidence interval explicitly shown; sample sizes are assay observations, not participant counts.

functional_evidence.evidence_location: Results, 'GRIN Variants Selected for Rescue Pharmacology in Triheteromeric NMDARs'; Supplemental Table S2; Table 1.
functional_evidence.assay: Glutamate and glycine potency in diheteromeric receptors; channel-blocker response in engineered GluN1/GluN2A/GluN2B triheteromeric receptors.
functional_evidence.model: Xenopus laevis oocytes; triheteromeric stoichiometry enforced with coiled-coil/ER-retention constructs and altered GluN2B C-terminus.
functional_evidence.triheteromeric_context: Variant-containing receptors were tested for inhibitor response; this is not a full multi-assay or synaptic charge-transfer LoF/GoF classification.
functional_evidence.uncertainty_note: Mean ± SEM unless confidence interval explicitly shown; sample sizes are assay observations, not participant counts.

integrated_function.source_classification: Gain-of-function in the tested receptor assay
integrated_function.evidence_location: Figure 5/Table 3 summary; charge-transfer ratios 7.9 and 6.2 of WT.
integrated_function.why: Both author-calculated charge-transfer ratios and several functional parameters are above WT in the tested diheteromeric assay. A separate engineered-triheteromeric study also reports enhanced agonist potency, but tests pharmacological inhibitor response rather than complete net function.

context_caveats: The reduced surface-expression ratio coexists with increased gating, potency and modeled charge transfer; do not interpret one parameter alone as net LoF.
Triheteromeric receptor results depend on engineered stoichiometry and construct context; no neuronal or clinical effect is established.
